document.title: Secretary of State Cable to Amembassy New Delhi: "Subject: Recent Demarches on Afghanistan and P.K. Kaul's Reaction"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Shultz's stern reply to Dean. U.S. encouraged Indian activism only to foster realism in Moscow, not to shape Afghan political arrangements. Indian outreach to factions and Zahir Shah is unwelcome, and he questions the reporting from New Delhi.

persons.name: Armacost
persons.role: US Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs; author of the eyes-only message to Ambassador Dean

mentions.quote: BYES ONLY FOR AMB. DEAN FROM ARMACOST

persons.name: John Dean
persons.role: US Ambassador to India, recipient of the cable

mentions.quote: 2. JOHN, NONE OF US IN WASHINGTON NEEDS TO BE REMINDED OF THE UTILITY OF KEEPING P.K. KAUL

persons.name: P.K. Kaul
persons.role: Indian Ambassador to the United States

mentions.quote: I HAVE DEVOTED QUITE A LITTLE TIME TO STROKING P.K. KAUL OVER THE PAST SEVERAL YEARS
WILL SEE HIM AGAIN ON FEBRUARY 12 AT HIS REQUEST

persons.name: Rajiv Gandhi
persons.role: Prime Minister of India, visited Washington

mentions.quote: HOUSTON CONSULATE TO BOLSTER HIS POSITION WHEN RAJIV VISITED

persons.name: K.P.S. Menon

events.description: Edward Djerejian met P.K. Kaul after reports of Natwar Singh's intended meeting with Zahir Shah.
Armacost to meet P.K. Kaul at Kaul's request.
Secret cable from Shultz/Armacost to Ambassador Dean on demarches to India regarding Afghanistan.
Armacost met K.P.S. Menon during Rajiv Gandhi's visit to Washington, urging India to continue Kabul dialogue.
Edward Djerejian met P.K. Kaul over reports of Natwar Singh's intended meeting with Zahir Shah.
Armacost planned to meet P.K. Kaul at Kaul's request.
Secretary of State cable to Embassy New Delhi on Indian activities regarding Afghanistan.
Gorbachev issued a statement on Afghanistan, prompting Kaul to phone Armacost earlier that week.
Armacost met K.P.S. Menon during Rajiv Gandhi's visit to Washington, encouraging Indian ambassador in Kabul to keep talking with Jon Glassman.

relationships.detail: Kaul is an Indian government official dealing with the US (likely ambassador to the US).
relationships.quote: KEEPING P.K. KAUL IN A CONSTRUCTIVE FRAME OF MIND

key_claims: The US encouraged India to talk to Moscow and Kabul but not to operationally shape Afghanistan's internal political arrangements.
Indian contacts with certain resistance leaders aroused intense suspicion among Pakistanis and mujahidin leaders during interim government negotiations.
Indian interest in Zahir Shah weakened his credibility with key players in Islamabad and Peshawar, diminishing his prospects in a transition.
Armacost accused the New Delhi embassy of misunderstanding US requests to India and urged a stronger defense of US interests.
